items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1958-Fall
items.q: I wrote the words to two of them... he nominated me... the first thing started on those songs was, uh, was a tune that he wrote for a clarinet player

ctx.x: Uh, well, no, not really often, and, uh, still I did go a fair number of times, you know, because after, after a couple of months we got started in trying to get these pieces out for him, you know, those four, four first songs. If you knew, and so. Yeah, no, and, uh, we were working on those, I, I wrote the words to two of them, you know, and tried to, you know, you nominated me, right over there. This is Tony. No, no, it's a general.
Tony Earne. Oh, which one of the two that you wrote the words for? If you knew, and why? That's right, if you knew.

And I wrote the verse to Sweet Substitute, but I didn't claim it, I think I should claim it. I think he should claim it. Oh, yeah. It's a good one. He would, uh, yeah, it's getting a little popularity. Mm-hmm. But, uh, funny, funny thing about it, I say he, he nominated me, I said, well, I said, get Sidney Martin, I said, the, the first thing started on those songs was, uh, was a tune that he wrote for a clarinet player that he wanted to record with. Here? Yes. I don't know that played in an orchestra, and I…
